project: Brain Feature — Port from Nexus to Vibey v2
description: Port the Brain feature into Vibey v2. NestJS brain module connects to NeuralSnap Supabase (lmwfgqhtogjbqpvzckua). Two consumers: frontend user (JWT) + Vibey agent on VM (service token). Frontend ports The-Nexus brain visualization.

context.currentProblem: Brain page is a placeholder. Complete brain system exists on VM (nexus-api) and NeuralSnap Supabase. Need to wire NestJS as single gateway for both frontend and agent.
context.desiredState: Brain page with graph visualization, memory CRUD, neural snapshot crystallization. Vibey agent on VM can save/search memories through NestJS. All brain data in NeuralSnap Supabase.
context.architectureGoal: NestJS brain module uses second Supabase client (NeuralSnap). Two auth paths: user JWT for frontend, service token for Vibey agent. Migrate missing tables (memories, memory_connections, etc.) into NeuralSnap Supabase alongside existing ns_* tables.

userStories.title: Migrate missing tables + RPCs into NeuralSnap Supabase
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the memories tables and RPC functions in NeuralSnap Supabase so the brain module can store raw memories alongside crystallized snapshots.
acceptanceCriteria: Table 'memories' created in NeuralSnap Supabase (lmwfgqhtogjbqpvzckua) with all 20 columns matching Nexus schema
RPC function 'search_memories' created (pgvector cosine similarity search)
RPC function 'search_neural_snapshots' created (uses existing ns_snapshots + pgvector)
RLS policies on new tables: owner-based access via auth.uid()
All migrations applied via Supabase MCP apply_migration
userStories.notes: NeuralSnap already has pgvector v0.8.0 and 13 ns_* tables. We ADD 4 new tables + RPCs alongside them. Schema verified from Nexus Supabase hmjnnznghncnyfrryssp. The memories table uses 768-dim vectors from Gemini embedding model.

userStories.title: Create NeuralSnap Supabase client in NestJS
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a second Supabase client in NestJS that connects to NeuralSnap Supabase for brain operations.
acceptanceCriteria: Creates Supabase client using NEURALSNAP_SUPABASE_URL + NEURALSNAP_SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY env vars
NEURALSNAP_SUPABASE_URL and NEURALSNAP_SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY added to apps/api/.env.example
Service is injectable via NestJS DI
Does NOT interfere with existing Vibey2.0 Supabase client (used by conversations, campaigns)
userStories.notes: This is a service-role client (not per-user JWT) because NeuralSnap Supabase has different auth than Vibey2.0 Supabase. Brain data is scoped by user_id in RLS, but the client authenticates with service key.

userStories.title: Create Brain NestJS module with types + dual auth
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the Brain module skeleton with types and a guard that accepts both user JWT and agent service token.
acceptanceCriteria: apps/api/src/modules/brain/types/brain.types.ts defines all types matching both memories and ns_snapshots schemas
apps/api/src/modules/brain/guards/brain-auth.guard.ts accepts: (a) Supabase JWT from Authorization header, (b) service token from X-Agent-Token header
Service token loaded from BRAIN_AGENT_TOKEN env var
Guard attaches user_id to request context (from JWT or from a configured agent user_id)
userStories.notes: Two auth paths: frontend sends Supabase JWT (existing pattern), Vibey agent on VM sends X-Agent-Token header. Both resolve to a user_id that scopes all brain queries.

userStories.title: Port memories CRUD (repository + service + controller)
userStories.description: As a user/agent, I need API endpoints to create, read, update, delete, and search memories.
acceptanceCriteria: Repository uses NeuralSnap Supabase client (not Vibey2.0 client)
POST /api/brain/remember — store memory with content_hash dedup
POST /api/brain/search — semantic search via search_memories RPC
GET /api/brain/stats — counts by type/source, connections, most recalled
userStories.notes: Port from nexus-api/src/routes/brain.ts. Embedding generation deferred to US-007. Connection discovery deferred to US-006.

userStories.title: Port neural snapshots CRUD (repository + service + controller)
userStories.description: As a user/agent, I need API endpoints for crystallized neural snapshots.
acceptanceCriteria: Repository reads/writes ns_snapshots table in NeuralSnap Supabase
GET /api/brain/snapshots — list with filters (type, tag, min_confidence, limit)
GET /api/brain/snapshots/search — semantic search via search_neural_snapshots RPC
GET /api/brain/snapshots/stats — count by type, avg confidence
All queries scoped by brain owner (ns_brains.owner_id = user_id)
userStories.notes: Port from nexus-api/src/routes/snapshots.ts. Uses existing ns_snapshots table (29 cols). Crystallization pipeline is US-008.

userStories.title: Port graph endpoint + memory connections
userStories.description: As a frontend, I need the graph data endpoint that powers the ForceGraph visualization.
acceptanceCriteria: Nodes include: enriched memories (age_category, status, node_type), document virtual nodes, neural snapshot nodes
Graph supports query params: limit, min_significance, memory_type
userStories.notes: Port from brain.ts GET /graph. Complex endpoint — merges memories + documents + snapshots into a unified graph. This is what the ForceGraph component consumes.

userStories.title: Add Gemini embedding service
userStories.description: As the system, I need embeddings generated for memories and snapshots to enable semantic search.
acceptanceCriteria: getEmbedding(text) returns number[] (768-dim) via Gemini gemini-embedding-001
Graceful fallback: returns null if key missing or API fails, flags needs_embedding in metadata
Integrated into memories create/update and snapshots create/update
userStories.notes: Requires GEMINI_API_KEY in apps/api/.env. Port from nexus-api getEmbedding helper.

userStories.title: Port crystallization pipeline
userStories.description: As a user/agent, I need the 4-phase pipeline that turns raw text into structured neural snapshots.
acceptanceCriteria: Phase 1 (parallel): Thought Extractor + Origin Mapper via Gemini
userStories.notes: Port from snapshots.ts POST /crystallize. 4 Gemini calls. Port prompts exactly.

userStories.title: Port conversation processing endpoint
userStories.description: As the Vibey agent, I need to send conversation transcripts to NestJS and have significant knowledge extracted into memories.
acceptanceCriteria: LLM extracts significant knowledge (strict filter prompt)
userStories.notes: Port from brain.ts POST /process/conversation. This is the key endpoint the Vibey agent calls after conversations to auto-learn. The extraction prompt is very detailed — port it exactly.

userStories.title: Port Brain frontend (types + service + store + visualization)
userStories.description: As a user, I need the Brain page with ForceGraph visualization, memory panel, stats, and detail modal.
acceptanceCriteria: apps/web/src/features/brain/ created with: types, services, store, components
API service uses backendClient pattern pointing to /api/brain/* endpoints
Zustand store manages graph data, selected node, filters, loading states
Adapted to Vibey design system (globals.css, Lucide icons)
userStories.notes: Port from The-Nexus/app/src/features/brain/. Adapt Phosphor → Lucide, Tailwind 4 → Vibey Tailwind config, React 19 patterns → current React.

visualVerification.lookFor: Force-directed graph with colored nodes, memory panel, stats bar. Not 'Coming soon' placeholder.

userStories.title: Wire Brain page + replace placeholder
userStories.description: As a user, I need /brain to show the complete Brain feature.
acceptanceCriteria: Page loads graph data on mount

visualVerification.lookFor: Complete Brain page. Graph, stats, memory panel all functional.
